blocks.prompt: 4. A particle moving along a coordinate line at time \(t = 0\) is at a position 2 cm from the origin and traveling at a velocity of 5 cm/sec. If the acceleration of the particle is given by \(a(t) = 3 - 4(t + 2)^{-3}\), find the velocity and the position of the particle as functions of \(t\).
blocks.explanation:
Is sawal mein do dafa integrate karna hai: acceleration se velocity, phir velocity se position. Har dafa ek naya constant aayega.
Diya kya hai? \(t = 0\) par position 2 cm aur velocity 5 cm/s, aur \(a(t) = 3 - 4(t+2)^{-3}\).
Rule kaunsa? \(v = \int a\,dt\), \(s = \int v\,dt\), aur \((t + 2)^{n}\) par power rule.
Plan: pehle \(v\) aur \(v(0) = 5\) se \(c_1\); phir \(s\) aur \(s(0) = 2\) se \(c_2\).
steps:
Diya gaya: \(a(t) = 3 - 4(t + 2)^{-3}\), \(v(0) = 5\) cm/s, \(s(0) = 2\) cm.
Maloom karna: \(v(t)\) aur \(s(t)\).
Tareeqa: \(v = \int a\,dt\), \(s = \int v\,dt\); do shuru wali values do constants tay karti hain.

Acceleration ko integrate karein
\[v(t) = \int\big(3 - 4(t + 2)^{-3}\big)\,dt\]
\[= 3t - 4\cdot\dfrac{(t + 2)^{-2}}{-2} + c_1\]
\[= 3t + \dfrac{2}{(t + 2)^{2}} + c_1\]
Kyun: \(\int (t + 2)^{n}\,dt = \frac{(t + 2)^{n+1}}{n + 1}\), yahan \(n = -3\), to power \(-2\) ho gayi aur \(-2\) se divide hua. Andar wale \(t + 2\) ka derivative 1 hai, is liye koi aur factor nahin aata.
Dhyan dein: \(-4 \div -2 = +2\); sign yahin palat jata hai.

Velocity ko integrate karein
\[s(t) = \int\left(3t + 2(t + 2)^{-2} + \dfrac{9}{2}\right)dt\]
\[= \dfrac{3}{2}t^{2} + 2\cdot\dfrac{(t + 2)^{-1}}{-1} + \dfrac{9}{2}t + c_2\]
\[= \dfrac{3}{2}t^{2} - \dfrac{2}{t + 2} + \dfrac{9}{2}t + c_2\]
Kyun: phir wahi power rule, ab \(n = -2\), to power \(-1\) aur \(-1\) se divide. Constant \(\frac{9}{2}\) ka integral \(\frac{9}{2}t\).

\(s(0) = 2\) lagayein
\[2 = 0 - \dfrac{2}{2} + 0 + c_2 \Rightarrow c_2 = 3\]
\[s(t) = \dfrac{3}{2}t^{2} + \dfrac{9}{2}t - \dfrac{2}{t + 2} + 3\]
Kyun: \(t = 0\) par \(\frac{2}{t + 2} = 1\), to \(2 = -1 + c_2\).
Dhyan dein: yahan \(c_2 = 2\) likh dena aam ghalti hai; \(-\frac{2}{t+2}\) wala term \(t = 0\) par zero nahin hota.

Tasdeeq
\[s'(t) = 3t + \dfrac{9}{2} + \dfrac{2}{(t + 2)^{2}} = v(t)\;\checkmark\]
\[v'(t) = 3 - \dfrac{4}{(t + 2)^{3}} = a(t)\;\checkmark\]
\(v(0) = \frac{1}{2} + \frac{9}{2} = 5\) aur \(s(0) = -1 + 3 = 2\;\checkmark\). Differentiate kar ke wapas wahi mil gaya jo diya tha.
